item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Withholding or continuing glucose-lowering drugs for elective surgery in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: withholding or continuing perioperative metformin. Responses to Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1280–1 and Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1282–3
item.description: We read with interest the correspondence pieces from Chen and colleagues1 and Wu and Li2 regarding our observational study on withholding or continuing metformin and other non-insulin glucose-lowering drugs in patients with diabetes mellitus undergoing surgery.3 In response, we revisited our Management and Outcomes of the Perioperative Care of European Patients with Diabetes (MOPED) database4 to address the effect of renal impairment among patients on metformin on days alive and at home within 30 days (DAH-30)5 and whether withholding metformin influences this further.

item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Differential effects of prone positioning and PEEP on ventilation/perfusion distribution across inflammatory ARDS subphenotypes: a porcine experimental study
item.description: ARDS comprises distinct inflammatory subphenotypes, including hyper- and hypo-inflammatory forms. Whether these differ in ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) mismatch and response to ventilatory strategies remains unclear. Dual-energy CT enables regional assessment of aeration and perfusion. This experimental study aimed to compare V/Q mismatch between hyper- and hypo-inflammatory subphenotypes, and respective responses to PEEP and prone positioning.
